    Topic 1: Fundamentals overview

    By the end, you will be able to

    • Describe the edit, compile, and run cycle.
    • Run and change a small Rust program.
    • Follow the module learning path toward a tested number summary.

    Prerequisite: Module 0 setup and Hello World.

    From source to a running program

    Rust source describes the steps a program should perform. The compiler checks that source and creates an executable; running the executable performs those steps. Cargo automates the build and run workflow for projects.

    flowchart LR
    A[Edit Rust source] --> B[Compile and check types]
    B --> C[Run executable]
    C --> D[Observe output]

    When does a compiler type error need to be fixed?




    A small runnable program

    main is the entry point. println! writes a line to the terminal; the exclamation mark identifies a macro. The double-quoted text is a string literal.

    fn main() {
    println!("Hello, fundamentals!");
}

    Run from the repository root:

    rustc examples/01-fundamentals/01-fundamentals-overview/main.rs -o /tmp/rust-fundamentals-intro
/tmp/rust-fundamentals-intro

    Expected output: Hello, fundamentals!.

    Which part begins execution in this program?




    Learning path and exercise

    • Topics 2–4 introduce bindings, types, collections, and text.
    • Topics 5–7 add functions, decisions, patterns, and repetition.
    • Topic 8 combines them in the tested number-summary Cargo project.

    Change the greeting to include your name. Predict the output, compile again, and run. Then remove the closing quote, read the diagnostic, and restore it. Detailed ownership rules come in Module 2; this module first builds the syntax and workflow needed to understand those rules.
